topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text: I opened the door to find a box sitting there, a little lopsided, its address label pointing accusingly at me. It wasn’t my name, though. The handwriting was unfamiliar, the name belonging to the person who once called this place home before I did. A mix of curiosity and a sense of responsibility tingled inside me. I decided it was important to do the right thing. After all, this package could contain anything—something essential, perhaps. I took a moment to jot down a note for the sender, explaining the mix-up gently, and added my new address, just in case. Then, carefully, I packed it back up, securing the flaps with fresh tape. Off to the post office it went, back into the world with a new direction. It felt good to know I’d helped keep the cycle of delivery going, even if just a small part of it.
